chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about a man in a state of Ihram who had intercourse with his slave girl who was in a state of Ihram.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Is he financially solvent or insolvent?' I said, 'Answer me regarding both of them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Did he instruct her to enter Ihram, or did he not instruct her, or did she enter Ihram on her own accord?' I said, 'Answer me regarding both of these [scenarios].'

So he (peace be upon him) said, 'If he was financially solvent and knew that it was not befitting for him, and he was the one who instructed her to enter Ihram, then upon him is a camel; and if he wishes, a cow, or if he wishes, a sheep. And if he did not instruct her to enter Ihram, then there is nothing upon him, whether he was financially solvent or insolvent. And if he instructed her and he was financially insolvent, then upon him is the blood of a sheep or fasting.'

key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: The blood of a sheep (a type of sacrifice)
key_terms.مُحِلٍّ: A man who is in a state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.مُحْرِمَةٍ: A female slave in a state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man having intercourse with his slave girl while she is in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the variable expiation (kaffarah) for a man in a state of non-Ihram having intercourse with his slave girl who is in Ihram, distinguishing penalties based on his financial status and whether he initiated her Ihram. It highlights the Shia juristic nuance that if he was solvent and commanded her to enter Ihram, he bears a heavier penalty (a camel, cow, or sheep), whereas if he was insolvent or did not command her, the liability is lighter or non-existent. This ruling underscores the principle that intention and agency in the act of entering Ihram significantly influence the legal consequence in marital relations during Hajj.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Sabbah Al Haza’a, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws, ‘Inform me about a man not in Ihraam falling upon a slave girl of his in Ihraam’. Heasws said: ‘Is he (financially) solvent or insolvent?’ I said, ‘Answer me regarding both of them’. Heasws said: ‘Did he instruct her to be in Ihraam or did not instruct her so? Or did she wear Ihraam of her own accord?’ I said, ‘Answer me regarding both of these’.

So heasws said: ‘If he was (financially) solvent and was knowing that it is not befitting for him, and he had instructed her to be in Ihraam, so upon him is a sacrificial animal; and if he so desires it, a cow, or if he so desires it, a sheep. And, if he did not happen to have instructed her with the Ihraam, so there is nothing upon him, whether he was (financially) solvent or insolvent; and if he had instructed her so and he was (financially) solvent, so upon him is blood of a sheep, or Fasts’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Sabbah al-Hadhdha’ from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is not in the state of Ihram and involves himself in sexual relation with his slave-girl who is in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is he affluent or poor?’ I replied, ‘I am a stranger about his condition.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Did he command her to assume the state of Ihram or she did it on her own?’ I replied, ‘I am stranger about it.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘If he is affluent and knowing that he must not have done so and he was the one who commanded her to assume the state of Ihram, he owes one badanah or if he likes one cow or one sheep. If he did not command her to assume the state of Ihram, he then does not owe anything, regardless of being affluent or poor, but if he had commanded her to assume the state of Ihram and he is poor, he then owes one sheep.’”
